actor_instance: Owner-pasted Magnolia job 576517 accounting and output, reviewed by Codex
goal: Provide a same-UID P2 network isolation path on Magnolia's legacy util-linux without weakening the private teacher corpus gate.
procedure: Record the observed util-linux 2.23.2 missing --map-current-user. In a single host Python process call unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET); write a one-line original-UID identity map, deny setgroups, and write the original-GID identity map before exec. Verify maps, nonzero caller, separate network namespace and lo-only interfaces; close inherited descriptors above standard streams. Run the actual P2 container check in a no-data Slurm job. Use the same helper in the teacher CPU script, but enter it before any private manifest is resolved or hashed and keep the P2 guard inside.
decision_criteria: stdout reports unshare from util-linux 2.23.2, host UID 1905 and GID 100
stderr reports missing --map-current-user and direct --net EPERM
three local focused helper tests passed; both Slurm scripts passed bash -n; local root-caller rejection passed
authority: The owner-pasted logs establish the legacy CLI limitation. The new syscall helper is published and tested locally for guard behavior, but no Magnolia execution of that helper or P2 isolation receipt exists. No teacher corpus processing, trained weights or product capability follows.
validation: Compared owner-pasted job 576517 outputs to published script; reviewed Linux user namespace map ordering; ran three focused mock/fail-closed tests and shell syntax checks, then verified published MFM tree. The original Magnolia files were not fetched.
failure_or_lesson: A CLI capability gap can be worked around by an identity mapping before exec in a single process, but only the measured no-data P2 probe can authorize the private CPU lane. A successful namespace syscall alone is insufficient.
